comment: The notification gate (plan §2.1), shared by notify.rs (Mac) and sparkbox_agent.py (agent).
Times: t is in seconds (unix seconds when quiet hours are set); feed the gate t*1000 ms.
Runner: group events by t, in order. For each t: if a 'tick' event is there, tick(t) first;
then decide() the other events in file order; then flush(t + 10 s) (the group window).
'outcomes' are the outcomes of that t's alert events in order (ack, tick, silence and
maintenance events have none); 'messages' are what the flush sent, in order. A message's
'lines' are checked only where the expectation lists them.
silence {rule|null, entity, reason}: from t on, events on that entity (and rule, unless null)
are marked silenced. maintenance {node, until, reason}: events whose node is that node are
marked planned while t < until. ack {rule, entity}: no more repeats for that key.
Message titles: a single alert's message is its event title; a repeat is 'Still firing: ' +
the title it was raised with ('Still flapping: ' once it has flapped); coalesced alerts are listed in their incident's next message
as 'Also: ' + title; an incident with several sends in one window is one message titled by
its worst item, the others as lines; more than 2 messages in one flush become one grouped
message '<n> alerts, <c> critical' (', <r> cleared' when resolutions are in it; '<n> alerts'
with no critical) whose lines are every critical title, then warnings, then resolutions, at
most 6, then 'and <k> more'.
Flap damping (G16): the resolve of anything paged, except a node back online (G16b), waits until it has stayed clear for flapS (10 min): its outcome
is held, and the first tick at or after that time sends it (its title, its severity; in quiet hours only when
what was paged was critical). A raise of the same K before then, at a severity no higher than what was paged,
is flapping: not sent, and the earlier clear is never sent. A raise above what was paged is an escalation and is
sent. A resolve still waiting when K is raised after flapS is dropped, and that raise is a new page. A tick sends
Back online (G16b): the resolve of a paged node-offline or peer-unreachable is sent at once, never held (quiet hours
included, since what was paged was critical). Raised again within flapS of a return that was told, at no more than
what was paged, it's paged again; the second such raise as '<title> · flapping'. After that, a raise within flapS
of its last return is flapping (not sent) and its return is not-paged, until it stays away flapS: then the first
tick at or after that sends 'Still flapping: <title>' (its severity; a warning not in quiet hours or with critical
only), and its return is sent again. A repeat also counts as telling it's away. A raise more than flapS after its
last return is a new page; a tick sends nothing for a return.
due resolves before repeats.
Quiet-hours digest (G15): a tick notes whether quiet hours are on. At the first tick after they end, the warnings
held for quiet hours that are still firing (not silenced, not planned) go out as one message 'While quiet: <n>
warning(s) still firing' (warn), its lines their titles (at most 6, then 'and <k> more'); they count as paged
from then on. Not with critical only. The digest comes after the flush's other messages.
paged {incident, severity, title, by} (G17): another sender (a node's agent) paged that incident at t. Here it
counts as paged: a warning in it within 30 min is coalesced and listed in this sender's next message about it.
